decision: Archive (Swift 6 strict concurrency) is stricter than SwiftPM CI — verify via deploy-dryrun

Fix: declare title/description/openAppWhenRun as 'static let'. General lesson: green ci.yml does NOT guarantee a green archive; the device Release archive catches concurrency/strictness ci.yml misses.
expected_outcome: Before any deploy, run the build_only dryrun (HEAD:deploy-dryrun) to catch archive-only failures without burning the daily upload quota. Keep AppIntent/protocol static requirements immutable (let).

decision: Daily TestFlight upload cap exhausted by auto-merge -> main auto-upload

decision: TestFlight build 1837 VALID — token-free deploy proven end-to-end

The pure estimator is unit-test-verified correct for clean/noisy/random/flat synthetic signals (PulsePeriodEstimatorTests), so the field nil is data/rate dependent (the real bandpassed window or a true frame rate far from the 15 Hz the bandpass is tuned for), not a generic bug. decision: rPPG root cause = 7.5 Hz rate broke the 15 Hz-designed bandpass (Nyquist); fixed rate-correctly
reasoning: The v10.72.1 rate/win telemetry revealed the camera delivers ~15 fps but the analyzer decimated by 2 → 7.5 Hz, while the Butterworth bandpass was hardcoded for 15 Hz. At 7.5 Hz the 4.0 Hz low-pass exceeds the 3.75 Hz Nyquist → tanf prewarp negative → invalid filter → acf=0 all session, confidence capped 0.27 < the 0.35 publish threshold, so the camera pulse NEVER reached the bus (rPPG effectively non-functional). Fix (CameraAnalyzer, dsp-reviewed, Rausch triad untouched): process every frame (no decimation), clamp low-pass to 0.45·rate (never above Nyquist), and re-tune the bandpass once to the TRUE measured frame rate. Correct at any fps; unchanged on a clean 15 Hz device.
expected_outcome: Camera HR should finally lock + publish, driving sound/visual/light. Shipped v10.74.0. Confirm on next device session (watch acf>0, conf≥0.35, rate≈15).

decision: TestFlight deploy was BROKEN since the rPPG fix (builds 2032–2036 all failed); fixed a Swift init-order error
reasoning: Founder saw '10.65.0 (2031)' and asked 'kommt da noch was?'. Investigation (GitHub Actions logs) revealed the last build that reached TestFlight was #2031 (v10.73.0); every build since the rPPG fix (#2032–#2036: rPPG, v10.75, panels, version bumps) FAILED to compile and silently never shipped. Single root cause: the rPPG fix turned CameraAnalyzer.effectiveSampleRate from let→var, and init() read self.effectiveSampleRate to build the bandpass coefficients before the last stored property (bpc) was initialized — Swift forbids self access before all stored properties are set. Confirmed via the latest failing run's full log that this was the ONLY compile error. Fix: read a static defaultSampleRate constant in init() instead of self. Shipped v10.76.3 (build 2037 — first green TestFlight since 2031).
expected_outcome: All queued work (rPPG lock fix, voice core, value-field keypad, keep-awake, persistent HUD, non-modal panels, auto-versioning) finally reaches the device. Lesson: a green local mindset is not a green CI — verify the actual TestFlight run conclusion, not just HEAD gates.

decision: 10.76.3 launch crash = SwiftUI metadata stack overflow from over-deep body type; fixed with AnyView erasure
reasoning: Build 2037 compiled+shipped but crashed at launch (EXC_BAD_ACCESS/SIGSEGV in the Stack Guard region). Device crash report: the Swift type-metadata decoder infinitely recursed (swift_getTypeByMangledNameInContext → decodeMangledType ⇄ decodeGenericArgs) while SwiftUI instantiated the ScrollView's VStack content in EchoelStudioView.body. The root view's body had grown into one extremely deep nested generic type (each `some View` panel expands its sub-tree into the parent's metadata; ~18 chained .sheet/.fullScreenCover modifiers embed content types). The new quick-access HUD branch + .echoelSheetPanel() on 12 sheet contents tipped the aggregate type past what the runtime decoder can resolve without overflowing the 1 MB main-thread stack — compile-clean, launch-only. Fix: AnyView type-erasure boundaries at the heavy branches (ScrollView children, HUD, all sheet/cover contents) so the decoder hits a concrete non-generic type. code-reviewer PASS; bracket balance verified. Shipped v10.76.4 (build 2038).
expected_outcome: App launches again with all recent work. Lesson: EchoelStudioView.body is at the structural-complexity limit — keep new panels behind AnyView or extract into child View structs; do not add more inline branches/sheets to the root body.

decision: Bio visual: phase-accumulated rings + per-frame uniform easing to kill stutter; coherence-driven interference + breath bloom for depth
reasoning: Founder on 10.76.4: 'Die visuals ruckeln hin und her' + wants more variety/design/Wirkung/physical-analytical. Root cause of the stutter: the ring shader used sin(d·density − time×flashHz) with unbounded time, so any HR-frequency change multiplied the large time → the pattern snapped many cycles at once (amplified by the jumpy rPPG BPM). Fixes in MetalBioView (one file): (1) integrate an accumulated pulse phase on the CPU and read it in the shader (frequency change alters rate, not position); (2) ease every bio/look uniform per frame with a frame-rate-independent exponential glide (HR, colour, breath, coherence, density, spread, hue) so updates glide not snap, and a thermal FPS step no longer reads as a speed change; (3) removed an AnyView wrapper around the live MTKView cover (identity churn → stutter) — launch-crash erasures on ScrollView/HUD/sheets stay. Added physics/variety: a second interference ring system detuned by coherence (ordered at high coherence, turbulent moiré at low — a literal visual of bio coherence) + breath bloom. Flash-safety unchanged (≤2.5 Hz). Swift+MSL code-reviewed; struct layouts match.
